ACT I

SCENE I. A counting-house.

CLERK.
The ledger shows a balance of four hundred.
The quarter's rent is due upon the Friday.
The wool that came from Bristol is unsold.
The carrier wants his money for the carriage.

MASTER.
Four hundred will not cover half of it.
What of the debt that Hollis owes the house?

CLERK.
He sends word he will pay us in the spring.
He sent the selfsame word to us last spring.

MASTER.
Then write to him again, and copy out
The whole account, and set the total under,
And say that if the sum is not received
Before the quarter day we go to law.

CLERK.
I have already drafted such a letter.
It wants your hand and nothing else besides.

MASTER.
You are ahead of me in everything.
One day you will be sitting in this chair
And some poor clerk will draft your letters for you,
And you will wonder where the years have gone.

CLERK.
I hope to be more punctual than Hollis.

MASTER.
That is a low bar to be stepping over.
Bring me the pen. And bring the Bristol book.
If we must sell the wool at a loss, we sell it,
But I will know exactly what we lose.
